newsitem.title: USA: Clinton aides warn victory not a sure thing.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aides warn victory not a sure thing.

text.p: Two of President Clinton's lieutenants warned against overconfidence Thursday and called for a concerted effort to get out the Democratic vote Nov. 5.
"What we are concerned about these last two weeks is complacency," deputy campaign manager Alan Wheat said in a conference call to rural leaders. "We want to ask everyone to ignore the polls."
Clinton has held comfortable leads over Republican nominee Bob Dole throughout the campaign. The daily Reuters tracking poll gave Clinton a lead of about nine points Thursday.
"My first bit of advice is not be complacent," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on the conference call. "The electorate is volatile (but) the polls look good."

The Clinton-Gore campaign arranged the conference call to 1,000 supporters to announce formation of "Rural Citizens for Clinton-Gore," a group of about 1,500 people. Glickman said the group "will try to get out the vote" in rural America.
